tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask one whole sports betting price question in plain English, the way a person would: which book pays the most for a bet, hedge math on a ticket, a parlay price, a game's board, a past result or how a line has moved. Returns a plain-sentence answer, the time the prices were scanned and a link to the matching page on theoddsgap.com. When a question could mean more than one game, it returns the choices as plain text to ask again with. A percent above fair in an answer is how far a price sits above our fair price, not expected profit; a middle's figure is how far above or below break-even. Prices may have moved since the scan. Information only: it places no bets and gives no picks.

question.description: One whole question, for example 'where is the best price on the Lions moneyline' or 'hedge my Ravens ticket at +240 for $50'.

tools.name: calc
tools.description: Runs a betting calculation on numbers you supply: convert odds between formats, implied probability, payout on a stake, the no-vig price of two sides, hold, breakeven, a parlay of typed odds, or an arb or hedge split on typed prices. Uses only the numbers given, no market data.

text.description: The reader's words, with their numbers.

tools.name: site_info
tools.description: Explains a betting term or how The Odds Gap works (gap percent, matched lines, the exchange depth rule, Kalshi fees, why offshore books are left out, the site's tools), in the site's own words with a link to the page it comes from.

topic.description: A topic key, or omit to read the words.

tools.name: slate
tools.description: Lists the games in a window (tonight, tomorrow, a weekday or a date) for a league or one team, with the highest moneyline price we saw on each side and the time it was scanned. Prices may have moved since the scan.

books.description: The books this person actually has. Omit for the default set.

sport.description: League, e.g. nfl or college football.

text.description: The reader's words, for the window.

when.description: today, tonight, tomorrow, a weekday, weekend, or YYYY-MM-DD. Default the next 24 hours.

tools.name: game_lines
tools.description: One game's moneyline, spread or total: both sides on the consensus number, or which side the market has as the favorite. Name the game in plain words, for example Lions at Bears. Shows the scan time and a link to the game's page. Prices may have moved since the scan.

books.description: The books this person actually has. Omit for the default set.

favored.description: Who the market favors, as a price.

game.description: The game in plain words, for example 'Lions at Bears' or 'Yankees tonight'.

line.description: The spread or total the bet is at. Omit for a moneyline, or to use the consensus line.

markets.description: Game-line markets to show, both sides each.

side.description: home or away for a moneyline or spread; over or under for a total.

team.description: A known team with no game on the board.

tools.name: past_game
tools.description: A finished game: the final score, the closing spread and total, and the earliest line we recorded, with a link to the game's page. Never an upcoming game.

game.description: The game in plain words, for example 'Lions at Bears' or 'Yankees tonight'.

list_all.description: Every finished game in the window the words name.

text.description: The team or matchup, in the reader's words.

tools.name: team_record
tools.description: A team's finished games tracked on The Odds Gap and its next game. Not an official league record.

text.description: The reader's words, for an ATS, over/under or trends record.

tools.name: futures_odds
tools.description: Season-long futures such as the Super Bowl, World Series, Stanley Cup, NBA and college titles: the highest price we saw on a team, or the top of one futures market, with the scan time. Prices may have moved since the scan.

books.description: The books this person actually has. Omit for the default set.

compare.description: Books the person named, to say each one's price.

market.description: A market phrase, if it is separable from the rest of the sentence.

sport.description: The league, if no market is named.

stake.description: A stake to pay out at the best price.

team.description: One entrant, if they named one.

teams.description: Two or more entrants asked together.

text.description: The person's own words. This is what names the market, because a futures market has no id anybody would ever say out loud.

tools.name: player_prop
tools.description: One player's prop: the line the market is at and the highest price we saw on each side, with the scan time. The player must be on our props board. Prices may have moved since the scan.

books.description: The books this person actually has. Omit for the default set.

line.description: The line the person named, if they named one.

market.description: The prop market key, e.g. player_receptions or pitcher_strikeouts. Omit to be told what the board has for that player.

player.description: The player's name as the person typed it.

tools.name: arbs
tools.description: Spots where two books' prices on opposite sides of the same bet added up to less than 100 percent implied at the scan, with how a stake would split. Prices may have moved since the scan. An arb can close at any time.

books.description: The books this person actually has. Omit for the default set.

game.description: The game in plain words, for example 'Lions at Bears' or 'Yankees tonight'.

tools.name: middles
tools.description: Spread and total middles across sportsbooks at the scan: two numbers far enough apart that both bets could win. Its figure (ev_pct, labelled Above Break-Even) is how far the market's hit chance times the payout sits above or below what the tickets cost, not expected profit. Prices may have moved since the scan.

books.description: The books this person actually has. Omit for the default set.

game.description: The game in plain words, for example 'Lions at Bears' or 'Yankees tonight'.

pick.description: A number to put in place of one side of the last middle, for 'what if I took 144.5 instead' (prompt 194).

stake.description: The stake on each ticket, for hit and miss dollars.
